task.name: Test processes a dev agent spawns outlive the sprint that started them and go on consuming the host indefinitely
task.story_text:
## Observed

Test processes a dev agent spawns inside its sandbox outlive the sprint that created them, and go
on consuming the machine indefinitely.

Story `issue-2284`'s dev agent ran the project's own suite four times while working, three of them
with `pytest -n auto --dist worksteal`, concurrently. Those invocations never terminated. Thirteen
hours after the sprint completed and its worktree was deleted, the machine still carried:

```
40 processes, ~321% CPU total
parent 4129   13:20:23  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_story_budget_seam.py::...
parent 68119  13:56:07  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_story_budget_seam.py -q -n auto --dist
parent 71222  13:51:50  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_story_budget_seam.py -q -n auto --dist
parent 85040  13:41:11  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_story_budget_seam.py -q
```

The parents were alive, not orphaned children of a reaped tree, and every worker executed from
`.forge/worktrees/issue-2284/.venv` — a path that no longer exists, held open by the running
processes.

The effect was not confined to wasted CPU. Every gate run on this host afterwards competed with
roughly three cores of dead test workers: a `make gate` that normally completes in about 55
seconds took 181, and a wall-clock timeout test failed inside it while passing three times out of
three when run alone. That failure was read as a possible regression in an unrelated story. Every
run duration recorded during those thirteen hours — the same durations adaptive limits derive dev
timeouts from — was measured against a host under load that nothing accounted for.

## Expected

Work a sprint starts should not outlive the sprint. A story's agent runs inside a sandbox with a
worktree, a virtualenv and a budget, all of which end when the story does; a process it spawned is
part of that same envelope and should end with it, whether the story succeeded, failed, or was
stopped.

The failure is quiet in a way that matters. A leaked process produces no artifact, no cost record
and no log line, so nothing in the run reports it and nothing in a later run knows it is there.
What it changes instead is every timing measurement taken afterwards on the same host — which is
the input the system uses to decide how long work should be allowed to take. A leak that only
wasted CPU would be a nuisance; one that silently biases the measurements the scheduler learns
from is a correctness problem for everything measured while it persists.

That an agent runs the suite at all is reasonable and worth keeping. That it can run it several
times concurrently, each fanning out across every core, inside an environment already running
under the coordinator's own parallelism, is a resource decision nobody made — the agent has no way
to know what else is executing, so the bound has to come from the side that does.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** pytest processes spawned by a dev agent remain running and consuming CPU
  long after the sprint that started them has completed and its worktree has been removed.
- **Evidence:** four `pytest` parents with elapsed times of 13h20m–13h56m, PPIDs alive, and 40
  associated workers totalling ~321% CPU, all executing `.forge/worktrees/issue-2284/.venv/bin/python`
  after that worktree was deleted. Three carried `-n auto --dist worksteal`. The sprint that
  spawned them had completed and landed via #2285.
- **Ruled out:** not the 21-day-old orphaned `codex exec` pair from another project — those are
  idle, 13 minutes of CPU across 21 days, and unrelated.
- **Ruled out:** not a worktree-cleanup failure. The worktree was removed; the processes held the
  freed inode open, which is why they remained visible under a path that no longer resolves.
- **Confirmed cause:** processes started by an agent inside its sandbox are not part of anything
  the sprint tears down at story end, so a subprocess that does not exit on its own persists
  without limit.
- **Affected code path:** sandbox process supervision and story teardown.
- **Fix-success criterion:** a process a story's agent starts does not outlive the story, whatever
  the story's outcome, and a process that has to be terminated at teardown is recorded so the run
  shows it happened. The suite remains runnable by an agent; what it cannot do is leave work
  behind.

handoff.summary: Closed the lifecycle gap at the runner process-group boundary. release_group_record no longer assumes a clean CLI exit means the group went with it: it probes the group, snapshots membership, killpg-s any survivors, waits bounded, and returns a structured ProcessTeardown (killed_survivors or retained_for_reaper, with pgid, member count, sandbox dir and completion). Those facts propagate as a new AgentResult.process_teardown field from all three local CLI runners — Claude via a variable set in its finally and attached to each post-teardown return; Codex via a teardown_out out-parameter on run_in_process_group plus a dataclasses.replace graft onto the _handle_exception timeout result; Gemini by moving off bare subprocess.run onto run_in_process_group, which previously gave it no process group, no registry entry and no teardown at all. The audit writer records cost.agents[].process_teardown on every invocation (None meaning the group ended on its own, which is distinct from an older record that never asked), with CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 24, a _migrate_v23_to_v24 backfilling None, and the v24 snapshot committed. The coordinator's gate-shell path had the identical clean-exit assumption (make gate returning is not proof its pytest-xdist workers stopped) and is now routed through the same helper, which also removed duplicated retain/unregister logic. New tests/test_process_teardown_lifecycle.py covers the seam, all three runners, the gate shell, the audit record, the migration and the refused-kill retention path using real subprocesses via new grandchild_success fake-CLI modes; verified to fail against the pre-fix release semantics.

commits.message: fix(process): end a story's spawned process tree at the story, and record it

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A process a story's agent starts does not outlive the story, whatever the story's outcome.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Every CLI-backed invocation now verifies its process group is empty at release and kills survivors before the story proceeds — the clean-success path that previously deferred them to an opportunistic later reaper. Covered for all three local runners (claude/codex/gemini) plus run_in_process_group itself and the gate shell, with real-subprocess tests asserting the grandchild is gone after the runner returns while the result still reports success. The refused-kill case (sandbox denies killpg) still retains the sidecar for the orphan reaper, which remains the only honest outcome there.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A process that has to be terminated at teardown is recorded so the run shows it happened.
acceptance_criteria.notes: ProcessTeardown rides out on AgentResult.process_teardown and is rendered into the originating run's audit at cost.agents[].process_teardown with pgid, action, member count, member pids, sandbox path and whether cleanup completed or was retained for the reaper. Written on every agent entry (null when the group ended on its own) so absence-vs-null stays meaningful; record schema bumped to v24 with a migration and a regenerated snapshot. tests/test_process_teardown_lifecycle.py::test_forced_teardown_appears_in_the_run_audit pins it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The suite remains runnable by an agent; what it cannot do is leave work behind.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Nothing restricts what an agent may run. The only new behaviour is at teardown: the invocation's own success is preserved (tests assert result.success is True on the clean-exit-with-survivors path) and only its leftovers are killed.

story_deviations: Plan step 3 was labelled 'create' but audit_render.py / audit.py / audit_substrate.py already existed; treated as modify-plus-one-new-snapshot as the plan reviewer noted. SCHEMA_VERSION lives only in audit_substrate.py (audit.py re-exports it), so one bump covered both names.

Plan step 2 left the codex teardown channel unnamed. Chose the out-parameter the plan reviewer recommended (teardown_out on run_in_process_group) rather than changing its return type, which keeps the two existing mock targets in test_runner_codex.py and test_runner_providers.py working. The _handle_exception timeout result gets the metadata grafted on via dataclasses.replace in the runner rather than threading process-group knowledge into the transport-agnostic helper.

Extended scope by one file beyond the plan: coordinator/util.py's _run_shell_detailed, flagged as adjacent by both plan reviewers, carried the same clean-exit assumption for gate commands and is now routed through release_group_record. Cheap (it deleted duplicated logic) and in-scope under the in_scope P2 policy.

Did not add the #2115 _identity_verdict fingerprint check before the clean-release kill. The leader's fingerprint is unverifiable at that moment (it has just exited) and the check is unnecessary: a pgid cannot be reallocated while its group is non-empty, so enumerated live members are necessarily this group's. Documented in release_group_record's docstring.
deferred_items: The spec's Expected section argues an agent should not be able to run the suite several times concurrently at full fan-out and that the bound must come from the coordinator. That is a resource-policy decision, not a lifecycle one, and appears in no acceptance criterion or in the fix-success criterion — not implemented. Worth its own story if wanted.

Three existing test files (test_cut_rc_isolation.py, test_sprint_lock.py, test_sprint_reexec_collision.py — 17 tests) fail in this sandbox with PermissionError from multiprocessing.SemLock and mktemp. Pre-existing environment restriction, unrelated to any changed code path; expected to pass in the coordinator's gate.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the review's P1: a process group is escapable, so a process the agent starts that calls setsid left the registered pgid and outlived the story invisibly. Added a process lease — open_process_lease stamps a fresh, never-reused token into the child's environment at spawn, and because environment is inherited across fork/exec and survives setsid, every descendant carries it however many sessions deep. close_process_lease enumerates live holders (/proc/<pid>/environ on Linux, sysctl KERN_PROCARGS2 on macOS, skipping processes older than the lease so the sweep costs ~0.7ms) and kills them. release_group_record runs the group kill first, then the lease sweep, and now accepts pgid=None so the sweep still runs when the group could not be resolved. Wired at all four spawn sites: run_in_process_group (codex + gemini), the claude runner's own Popen, and the gate shell in coordinator/util.py. The token is also recorded on the reaper sidecar and swept by reap_orphan_agents regardless of the pgid verdict — it needs no identity check because a token minted once for one spawn cannot be counterfeited by a recycled id, unlike the pgid that #2115 guards. ProcessTeardown gained escaped_pids so the audit distinguishes a survivor that stayed in the group from one that stepped outside it; the v24 snapshot was regenerated (no version bump — v24 is introduced by this branch and has not shipped). Iteration 0's work is otherwise unchanged: clean-exit group verification, teardown facts on AgentResult, cost.agents[].process_teardown at schema v24 with the v23-to-v24 migration, and gemini moved onto the group-isolated spawn.

commits.message: fix(process): end a story's spawned process tree at the story, and record it
fix(process): contain descendants that leave the process group (iter 1)

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A process a story's agent starts does not outlive the story, whatever the story's outcome.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Two containers now, checked in order. The process group catches descendants that stayed in it (verified at release rather than assumed from a clean exit). The lease catches the ones that did not: a token inherited through environment, which setsid cannot shed. Both run at all four spawn sites — claude, codex, gemini and the gate shell — on success, timeout and unwind paths. Real-subprocess tests cover a same-group grandchild and a setsid escapee for each runner, plus inheritance through a multi-exec chain; all were verified to fail with the respective mechanism disabled.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A process that has to be terminated at teardown is recorded so the run shows it happened.
acceptance_criteria.notes: ProcessTeardown rides out on AgentResult.process_teardown into cost.agents[].process_teardown, now with escaped_pids alongside members so the record says which container caught what — a survivor that outran its invocation and one that also left the container it was placed in are different facts. Null on an invocation whose tree ended on its own, so absence-vs-null stays meaningful. Schema v24 with migration and regenerated snapshot.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The suite remains runnable by an agent; what it cannot do is leave work behind.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Nothing restricts what an agent may run, and every clean-exit test asserts result.success is True while its leftovers are killed. The lease is a per-spawn token, so one invocation's teardown provably cannot reach another's work — pinned by test_a_lease_never_matches_another_spawn.

story_deviations: The P1 fix stays inside the plan's approach (Step 1's 'kill any surviving descendants' extended to descendants the pgid cannot name) rather than adopting the reviewer's alternatives of an OS job object or cgroup, which are Linux-only and privilege-bearing. The env-lease is the portable form of the same containment and is the 'additional descendant tracking mechanism' the finding's fix note also offered.

Extended beyond the plan's file list by two adjacent paths, both for the same defect: coordinator/util.py's gate shell (flagged by both plan reviewers in cycle 0) and reap_orphan_agents, which had the identical escapee blind spot on the SIGKILL-ed-sprint path.

Regenerated the v24 schema snapshot for escaped_pids rather than bumping to v25: v24 is introduced by this branch and has never been written by a shipped writer, so there is no stored record at v24 to migrate from.
deferred_items: Two existing tests in test_sprint_terminal_lifecycle.py and one in test_process_group.py simulated a refused killpg while leaving per-pid kills working; the lease now ends those trees at release, so their stand-in sandbox was changed to deny the per-pid kill too — which is what 'teardown reached only the direct child' means. They still exercise the reaper path; the improved outcome is covered separately in test_process_teardown_lifecycle.py.

Cycle 1 P2 (deepseek): the gate shell's ProcessTeardown is still not surfaced in any audit field — _run_shell_detailed returns only ok/output/code/timed_out, and threading a teardown record through every gate caller into the validate block is a wider change than this finding warrants. The gate's leaked workers are killed either way, and the log line plus reaper sidecar remain. Worth its own story if the recording criterion is to extend to gate shells.

The spec's Expected section argues an agent should not be able to run the suite several times concurrently at full fan-out and that the bound must come from the coordinator. Still not implemented: it is a resource-policy decision, appears in no acceptance criterion, and is unrelated to the P1.

17 tests in test_cut_rc_isolation.py, test_sprint_lock.py and test_sprint_reexec_collision.py fail in this sandbox with PermissionError from multiprocessing.SemLock and mktemp. Pre-existing environment restriction, identical set and count as before this iteration; none touch changed code.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 (runner_codex teardown metadata): run_in_process_group returns a subprocess.CompletedProcess (process_group.py:134), which has nowhere to carry teardown facts, and its release_group_record call is inside a finally (line 133). 'Preserve equivalent metadata from run_in_process_group(...)' therefore needs a channel the plan does not name.
  Suggestion: Dev picks the channel at implementation time — an out-parameter, a returned tuple, or a small result wrapper. Note that changing the return type would touch the two mock targets at tests/test_runner_codex.py:28 and tests/test_runner_providers.py:20, so an out-param is the cheaper shape.

finding_registry.description: When a CLI-backed invocation starts a long-lived subprocess in its own process group and exits successfully, run_in_process_group returns success with no process_teardown while the subprocess remains running.

A gate command that leaves a descendant running has that descendant killed by release_group_record, but the forced teardown is not carried into the run's audit record, so the run does not show that the kill happened.

Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
